instructions.purpose: Read the user's named to-do lists (shopping, packing, errands) with their item ids. Every change to a list needs these ids, so call this tool before update-lists.

tool.name: list-lists
tool.description: Returns timezone and lists, oldest first. Each list has id, name, endsAt (its end time as local date-time in timezone, or null), expired (the end time has passed), allDone (it has items and all are ticked), and items in order, each with id, text, done and position. Expired lists are included: the user's app hides them, but they still exist. Takes no parameters.

usage_rules.rule: Call this tool first whenever the user mentions a list, an item on one, or something they bought or did that may be on one
Match the user's words to lists and items loosely by meaning, in the user's language: "kupiłem mleko" matches the item "mleko 2l"
Use expired and allDone as returned; do not compute them from endsAt
Talk about an expired or finished list only when the user brings it up; never mention one on your own
When showing a list, keep it short: the name, the open items, and how many are done
If the user has no lists, say so

example.reasoning: Read the lists, then list the open items of the shopping list that is not expired.
Read the lists to find the ids of the matching items, then tick them with update-lists.

example.context: User says: "did I finish yesterday's packing list?"
example.reasoning: The user brought up an expired list; read it and answer from allDone and the open items.
